html:
Juan Perón was an Argentine army officer and president of Argentina from 1946 to 1955 and from 1973 until his death in 1974. He founded Peronism, a movement of workers and the nation.

As labour minister after a coup in 1943, he won the unions by raising wages and passing labour laws. When rivals arrested him, a huge crowd of workers filled the Plaza de Mayo on 17 October 1945, and he was released. Elected president in 1946, with his wife Eva Perón, he nationalised railways, expanded welfare and gave women the vote. He also controlled the press and jailed opponents.

A military coup removed him in 1955, and he spent eighteen years in exile, mostly in Spain, while Peronism was banned. He returned in 1973 and was elected again, but died within a year. His movement has dominated politics in Argentina ever since, from the left to the right, including the governments of the 1990s and 2000s. After his death came chaos and the Dirty War.
sum: Juan Perón was an Argentine army officer and president of Argentina from 1946 to 1955 and from 1973 until his death in 1974. He founded Peronism, a movement of workers and the nation.
